items.name: COMP_LIMITS
items.doc: The legal range of each compressor field (engineering units). The widget clamps drags to these, `normalizeComp` enforces them, the row's codec refuses by them and the travel sheet publishes them. `default`/`defaultFrom` are the come-up values `defaultCompState` seeds a fresh strip with, read BACK from here rather than restated there.

items.name: PROGRAM_RELEASE
items.doc: The program-dependent release's model constants — the LA-2A's opto cell as DATA. `chargeMs`/`dischargeMs` are the word's memory constants, shared by every profile; each profile's `fastMs`, `slowMinMs`, `slowMaxMs` and `share` fit the unit's published two-stage recovery. Not operator controls: generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_PROGRAM_RELEASE_*`, which libomxdsp's `omx_env_program_release` reads.

items.name: COMP_KINDS

source.origin: the console engine's compressor kinds (limiter -> peak, comp -> rms); omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_dynamics_instance.h:84 the rms argument

items.doc: The compressor's character, which picks its detector: `comp` runs the RMS detector, `limiter` the peak detector. The console's comp row carries it (`CompState.kind`, `COMP_KINDS`) and comes up as `comp`.

items.name: DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLINGS

source.origin: the console engine's detector oversampling choices (auto, off, 4x), defaulting to auto; omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/omx_dyn.h:46-50 OMX_DYN_OVS_AUTO 0, _OFF 1, _X4 2, fx/omx_dynamics_instance.h:84 ovs_mode

items.doc: The compressor's detector oversampling: `auto` runs the control path at 4x only while the attack is faster than DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS, `off` never, `4x` always (omx-dsp's OMX_DYN_OVS_AUTO, _OFF and _X4, in that order, so the index mapping holds). The ids are the console's wire vocabulary (`CompState.detectorOversampling`, what the dynamics row's OPTIONS publishes and a session stores), so the console re-exports this set; it comes up `auto`.

items.name: DETECTOR_TOPOLOGY

source.origin: omx-dsp 91beb6d (lane/salvage-ssl-bus-comp) include/omxdsp/omx_dyn.h:60-68 OMX_DYN_TOPOLOGY_FEEDFORWARD 0, OMX_DYN_TOPOLOGY_FEEDBACK 1, the comp row's detectorTopology (the SSL bus compressor design); :86 a zeroed atom is feedforward

items.doc: Where the compressor's detector listens: `feedforward` hears the slot's input (or its key), `feedback` hears the slot's own pre-make-up output DYN_FB_LOOP_DELAY_SAMPLES late, through one envelope stage, and a keyed slot stays feed-forward (omx-dsp's OMX_DYN_TOPOLOGY_FEEDFORWARD 0 and _FEEDBACK 1, in that order; the set is named for its control, so C spells them OMX_DETECTOR_TOPOLOGY_*). The console's comp row carries it (`detectorTopology`) and comes up `feedforward`, so a zeroed atom is the compressor every slot runs.

items.name: DYN_FB_LOOP_DELAY_SAMPLES

source.origin: omx-dsp 91beb6d (lane/salvage-ssl-bus-comp) include/omxdsp/omx_dyn.h:72 OMX_DYN_FB_LOOP_DELAY_SAMPLES 1u, :164 the _Static_assert that the loop state holds one sample per leg

items.doc: The feedback detector's loop delay, in samples: the output y[n] depends on the gain at n, so the detector can only have heard y[n - 1]. Not a latency: the audio is never delayed by it. omx-dsp's feedback state holds exactly this many output samples per leg.

items.name: DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_LATENCY_SAMPLES

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed include/omxdsp/omx_oversampler.h:151 OMX_OVS_LATENCY_4X 72; the console engine's DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_LATENCY_SAMPLES

items.doc: What the 4x detector oversampling costs the strip it is engaged on, in samples: the causal linear-phase half-band's reach, by which the audio is delayed so the gain still lands on the sample it was computed from. A sample count, not a time: the same at every rate. omx-dsp's oversampler declares the same number as OMX_OVS_LATENCY_4X, and its comp and gate faces report it while 4x is engaged.
